Serves as the organization's subject matter expert in workforce analytics and human capital data, transforming workforce, operational, financial, economic, and organizational data into strategic insights that support executive decision-making.

Partners with HR leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to develop analytics that inform recruiting, retention, compensation, workforce planning, succession planning, employee demographics, organizational effectiveness, facilities management, space utilization, and other strategic initiatives.

Leads analytics projects that expand organizational reporting capabilities and improve data-driven decision-making. Serves as a trusted advisor by providing guidance on workforce metrics, reporting methodologies, dashboard functionality, and interpretation of analytics. Maintains appropriate confidentiality when handling sensitive employee and organizational information.

Applies advanced professional judgment to independently resolve complex analytical and operational challenges. Assignments require initiative, creativity, sound judgment, and collaboration while serving as an expert resource for workforce analytics and reporting.

Responsibilities

Job Description:

Data Management & Analysis:
Develops and advances a comprehensive workforce analytics program that improves data availability, automation, and decision support. Evaluates emerging analytics methodologies and technologies to recommend enhancements that strengthen organizational capabilities. Performs advanced data extraction, preparation, modeling, statistical analysis, forecasting, and visualization to address complex business challenges. Conducts workforce analyses supporting talent management, workforce planning, recruiting, compensation, retention, succession planning, diversity metrics, organizational effectiveness, facilities management, and space utilization. Identifies trends, risks, and opportunities, develops actionable recommendations, and partners with leadership to establish workforce metrics, KPIs, and reporting priorities.

Data Assets & Data Integrity:
Designs, builds, and maintains data assets for senior leadership decision support. Develops, analyzes, tests, modifies, standardizes, and documents data preparation, data validation, data model, data storage, and data automation processes. Promotes enterprise HR data governance standards, consistent metric definitions, and data quality practices across reporting tools, dashboards, and organizational units. Collaborates with HR, Finance, IT, and other departments, maintaining strong cross-functional relationships to facilitate consensus and ensure alignment and consistency of workforce data. Ensures the accuracy, completeness, reliability and relevance of data sets and data models.

Dashboard Development and Management:
Designs, develops, tests, deploys, and maintains dashboards, data visualizations, and business intelligence solutions that effectively communicate workforce insights to technical and non-technical audiences. Manages dashboard releases, data pipelines, system testing, usability improvements, and performance optimization. Troubleshoots technical issues, documents solutions, and recommends enhancements that improve usability, accessibility, and adoption.

Reporting:
Leads recurring and ad hoc workforce reporting (e.g., turnover, demographics, recruiting, succession planning) that provides leadership with timely, accurate, and actionable information. Supports executive-level reporting needs through development of concise and meaningful workforce analytics presentations and summaries. Develops standardized metrics, executive presentations, dashboards, and analytical reports while validating data quality and ensuring consistency across reporting products.

Data Consultation:
Serves as a strategic thought partner to the CHRO and HR leadership, in identifying opportunities to leverage workforce data to inform organizational and talent decisions. Works closely with leadership and staff to identify analytical requirements. Serves as a resource to management, responding to questions, providing guidance on best practices and approaches to modeling and analyzing data. Project & Documentation Management:
Leads analytics initiatives from planning through implementation, including deployment of new solutions, enhancement of existing capabilities, and continuous process improvement. Documents analytical methodologies, business processes, and technical standards to support sustainability and knowledge sharing.

Training Development & Support:
Builds organizational capability by mentoring colleagues, developing training resources, promoting adoption of analytics tools, and improving data literacy across HR and the broader organization.

Ensures that any privileged, sensitive, or confidential information is securely stored, disposed of, and transmitted according to the Institutional guidance.

Strong knowledge of current data analysis, statistical, and visualization techniques.
Advanced proficiency with business intelligence and data visualization platforms such as Tableau and/or Power BI, and data management platforms such as PoolParty.

Ability to influence stakeholders without formal authority.
Ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and build consensus.
Ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable insights for technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to communicate complex analytical concepts to executive audiences.
Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and presentation skills.
Excellent attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Ability to build effective working relationships across departments and with leaders at all organizational levels.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to present findings and recommendations to leadership audiences.

Experience:
Six years of related professional experience in workforce analytics, HR analytics, business intelligence, reporting, or data analysis, including experience developing complex queries, performing advanced data analysis, and building dashboards and visualizations. Experience working with HR data and HR systems strongly preferred.

None.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Master Data Specialist owns the accuracy, completeness, and governance of supply chain master data across the organization's ERP and business systems. This is a hands-on role in an organization that is actively building its data foundation: the analyst will not only maintain records but help define the standards, processes, and controls that do not fully exist today.
The role covers four core data domains — materials/items, vendors/suppliers, customers, and BOMs/routings — and requires someone comfortable working across multiple systems, executing high-volume data updates, and bringing structure where processes are still informal.

Key Responsibilities

Master Data Maintenance & System Updates

Create, update, extend, and deactivate master data records (items/materials, vendors, customers, BOMs, routings) across all ERP and connected systems.
Execute mass data updates and migrations using system tools, upload templates, and data-loading utilities; validate results before and after changes.
Ensure cross-system consistency: when a record changes in one system, verify and synchronize dependent systems and downstream processes.
Process master data change requests within defined SLAs, verifying completeness and required approvals before entry.

Data Quality & Cleansing

Run recurring data quality audits (duplicates, missing fields, inconsistent units of measure, invalid statuses, orphaned BOM components) and remediate findings.
Establish and maintain data quality KPIs and dashboards; report accuracy and completeness metrics to your manager on a defined cadence.
Lead data cleansing initiatives, including preparation for system implementations, upgrades, or acquisitions.

Governance & Process Development

Help define and document master data standards: naming conventions, field definitions, mandatory attributes, and approval workflows for each data domain.
Draft and maintain SOPs and work instructions for master data creation and change processes.
Act as gatekeeper: challenge incomplete or non-standard data requests and route them through the correct approval path.
Support the rollout of data governance practices to other departments (procurement, sales, finance, operations) that consume or submit master data.

Cross-Functional Support & Analysis

Serve as the primary point of contact for master data questions from procurement, planning, warehouse, sales, and finance teams.
Support ERP projects, integrations, and system testing where master data is involved (UAT, data validation, cutover support).
Produce ad hoc analyses and extracts (e.g., item usage, vendor rationalization, BOM cost roll-up inputs) as requested.

Qualifications

Required

2–5 years of hands-on experience in master data maintenance within a supply chain, manufacturing, or distribution environment.
Demonstrated experience performing master data creation and mass updates directly in at least one major ERP (e.g., SAP, Oracle/NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365); ability to learn additional systems quickly, as this role works across multiple platforms.
Working knowledge of at least two of the four data domains: material/item master, vendor master, customer master, BOMs/routings.
IA skills and Excel skills (lookups, pivot tables, data cleaning at scale); experience with data upload/import templates and validation.
High attention to detail with a documented track record of accuracy in high-volume data work.
Ability to write clear process documentation and communicate data standards to non-technical colleagues.

Preferred

Experience in an organization building master data governance from an early stage (defining standards rather than inheriting them).
Exposure to data quality or MDM tools, SQL, or Power BI/reporting tools.
Experience supporting an ERP implementation, migration, or consolidation.
Understanding of how master data drives downstream processes: MRP, procurement, costing, and order management.
APICS/ASCM (CPIM) or similar supply chain certification.

Competencies

Accuracy and rigor —
treats data errors as defects, not inconveniences.
Process orientation —
builds repeatable methods rather than one-off fixes.
Ownership —
follows issues to root cause across systems and departments.
Communication —
can explain data requirements to requesters and push back constructively on bad inputs.
Adaptability —
comfortable in a maturing organization where standards are still being defined.

Success Measures (First 12 Months)

Documented data standards and SOPs in place for all four data domains.
Baseline data quality audit completed for each domain, with a remediation plan and measurable improvement.
Master data change-request process defined, communicated, and adopted, with SLA tracking.
Cross-system data consistency checks established and running on a regular cadence.

Growth Path

This role is scoped at the analyst/specialist level with a defined path toward Senior Analyst or Master Data Manager as the organization's data governance function matures.

Position Summary

The Master Data Specialist owns the accuracy, completeness, and governance of supply chain master data across the organization's ERP and business systems. This is a hands-on role in an organization that is actively building its data foundation: the analyst will not only maintain records but help define the standards, processes, and controls that do not fully exist today.
The role covers four core data domains — materials/items, vendors/suppliers, customers, and BOMs/routings — and requires someone comfortable working across multiple systems, executing high-volume data updates, and bringing structure where processes are still informal.

Key Responsibilities

Master Data Maintenance & System Updates

Create, update, extend, and deactivate master data records (items/materials, vendors, customers, BOMs, routings) across all ERP and connected systems.
Execute mass data updates and migrations using system tools, upload templates, and data-loading utilities; validate results before and after changes.
Ensure cross-system consistency: when a record changes in one system, verify and synchronize dependent systems and downstream processes.
Process master data change requests within defined SLAs, verifying completeness and required approvals before entry.

Data Quality & Cleansing

Run recurring data quality audits (duplicates, missing fields, inconsistent units of measure, invalid statuses, orphaned BOM components) and remediate findings.
Establish and maintain data quality KPIs and dashboards; report accuracy and completeness metrics to your manager on a defined cadence.
Lead data cleansing initiatives, including preparation for system implementations, upgrades, or acquisitions.

Governance & Process Development

Help define and document master data standards: naming conventions, field definitions, mandatory attributes, and approval workflows for each data domain.
Draft and maintain SOPs and work instructions for master data creation and change processes.
Act as gatekeeper: challenge incomplete or non-standard data requests and route them through the correct approval path.
Support the rollout of data governance practices to other departments (procurement, sales, finance, operations) that consume or submit master data.

Cross-Functional Support & Analysis

Serve as the primary point of contact for master data questions from procurement, planning, warehouse, sales, and finance teams.
Support ERP projects, integrations, and system testing where master data is involved (UAT, data validation, cutover support).
Produce ad hoc analyses and extracts (e.g., item usage, vendor rationalization, BOM cost roll-up inputs) as requested.

Qualifications

Required

2–5 years of hands-on experience in master data maintenance within a supply chain, manufacturing, or distribution environment.
Demonstrated experience performing master data creation and mass updates directly in at least one major ERP (e.g., SAP, Oracle/NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365); ability to learn additional systems quickly, as this role works across multiple platforms.
Working knowledge of at least two of the four data domains: material/item master, vendor master, customer master, BOMs/routings.
IA skills and Excel skills (lookups, pivot tables, data cleaning at scale); experience with data upload/import templates and validation.
High attention to detail with a documented track record of accuracy in high-volume data work.
Ability to write clear process documentation and communicate data standards to non-technical colleagues.

Preferred

Experience in an organization building master data governance from an early stage (defining standards rather than inheriting them).
Exposure to data quality or MDM tools, SQL, or Power BI/reporting tools.
Experience supporting an ERP implementation, migration, or consolidation.
Understanding of how master data drives downstream processes: MRP, procurement, costing, and order management.
APICS/ASCM (CPIM) or similar supply chain certification.

Competencies

Accuracy and rigor —
treats data errors as defects, not inconveniences.
Process orientation —
builds repeatable methods rather than one-off fixes.
Ownership —
follows issues to root cause across systems and departments.
Communication —
can explain data requirements to requesters and push back constructively on bad inputs.
Adaptability —
comfortable in a maturing organization where standards are still being defined.

Success Measures (First 12 Months)

Documented data standards and SOPs in place for all four data domains.
Baseline data quality audit completed for each domain, with a remediation plan and measurable improvement.
Master data change-request process defined, communicated, and adopted, with SLA tracking.
Cross-system data consistency checks established and running on a regular cadence.

Growth Path

This role is scoped at the analyst/specialist level with a defined path toward Senior Analyst or Master Data Manager as the organization's data governance function matures.
